album.title: Radif of Persian Music on Setar II

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on C3 and dwells most on G in Chaharmezrab. The line peaks at G4 (401.9 Hz) at 2:12.0. It closes on G3, not the tonic (Eb4 → Eb4 → Gk3 → G3 → G3 → G3).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic C set in the catalog (Shur's finalis C (267.0 Hz), which Dashti shares (Farhat 1990, p. 39): three of the suite's five tracks voted it and the pitch set is Shur from it, with the 5th at both 646 and 700 cents. The vote picked the 5th above, Dashti's shahed (same page). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 200.1 Hz (G)
